dish.title: Dominican Mangú with Pan-Fried Eggs and Pickled Red Onions
dish.description: Green plantains boiled until soft and mashed smooth with olive oil and some of their cooking liquid, topped with quick vinegar-pickled red onions, served with pan-fried eggs and sliced avocado.

recipe_version.title: Dominican Mangú with Pan-Fried Eggs and Pickled Red Onions
recipe_version.description: Green plantains boiled until soft and mashed smooth with olive oil and some of their cooking liquid, topped with quick vinegar-pickled red onions, served with pan-fried eggs and sliced avocado.

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Cut the ends off the plantains, slit the skins lengthwise, peel, and cut into 2-inch pieces. Slice the onions into thin rings.

steps.title: Boil the plantains
steps.body: Put the plantains in a 6-quart pot with 10 cups water and 2 tsp salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, about 12 minutes, then cook until very tender, about 20 minutes. Reserve 1 cup of the cooking water and drain.

steps.title: Pickle the onions
steps.body: While the plantains boil, warm the remaining olive oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium, add the onions, and cook 3 minutes until just softened. Add the vinegar and 1/2 tsp salt, simmer 1 minute, and take off the heat to turn pink (overlap stated).

steps.title: Mash
steps.body: Mash the hot plantains in the pot with 1/4 cup olive oil, adding up to 1 cup reserved cooking water a splash at a time until smooth and fluffy, about 4 minutes. Cover to keep warm.

steps.title: Pan-fry the eggs
steps.body: Heat the neutral oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium. Crack in 4 eggs and pan-fry until the whites set and the edges turn lacy, about 3 minutes; season with pepper. Repeat with the remaining eggs.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Mound the mangú on plates, top with the pickled onions and their juices, and serve with two eggs and avocado slices each.
